chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever belittles a believer, whether poor or not poor, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will not cease to belittle him and be hostile to him until he retracts from his belittling of him.

key_terms.مَحْقَرَتِهِ: his act of belittling or contempt

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of belittling a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the gravity of *tadqir* (belittling) as a spiritual disease that invites divine reciprocal humiliation (*haqir*) and enmity (*maqit*). It highlights that this consequence applies universally to all believers, irrespective of their socioeconomic status, serving as a warning against arrogance rooted in worldly distinctions. The condition of repentance (*ruju'*) implies that this state is reversible through sincere humility and rectification of one's attitude.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Husayn Bin Usman, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who considers a Momin as insignificant, be he a poor or without poverty, Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic will not Cease to Look down at him Angrily until he retracts from his belittling him’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al- Hus,ayn ibn ‘Uthman from Muhammad ibn abu Hamza from those whom has mentioned (in his book) from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
Whoever looks down upon a believer, destitute or not, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, continues looking down upon him and hate him until he changes his attitude as such toward a believer.’”
